tax_year_start.label: Start of tax year 2026/27
tax_year_start.source_title: Rates and thresholds for employers 2026 to 2027 - GOV.UK
tax_year_start.note: UK tax year runs 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027.

tax_year_end.label: End of tax year 2026/27
tax_year_end.source_title: Rates and thresholds for employers 2026 to 2027 - GOV.UK

personal_allowance.label: Standard Personal Allowance (whole UK)
personal_allowance.source_title: Income Tax rates and Personal Allowances: Current rates and allowances - GOV.UK
personal_allowance.note: Same in 2025/26. Applies UK-wide (England, Wales, Northern Ireland and Scotland). Frozen until 5 April 2031 (see thresholds_frozen_until).

personal_allowance_taper_threshold.label: Adjusted net income above which the Personal Allowance is reduced
personal_allowance_taper_threshold.source_title: Income Tax rates and Personal Allowances: Current rates and allowances - GOV.UK
personal_allowance_taper_threshold.note: Personal Allowance falls by GBP 1 for every GBP 2 of adjusted net income above GBP 100,000. Creates an effective 60% marginal band (rUK) between 100,000 and 125,140.

personal_allowance_taper_rate.label: Personal Allowance withdrawal rate (GBP 1 per GBP 2 above the taper threshold)
personal_allowance_taper_rate.source_title: Income Tax rates and Personal Allowances: Current rates and allowances - GOV.UK

personal_allowance_nil_at.label: Adjusted net income at which the Personal Allowance is fully withdrawn
personal_allowance_nil_at.source_title: Income Tax rates and Personal Allowances: Current rates and allowances - GOV.UK

thresholds_frozen_until.label: Personal Allowance, basic rate limit and equivalent NIC thresholds frozen until
thresholds_frozen_until.source_title: Income Tax: Maintaining the Personal Allowance and the basic rate limit for Income Tax, and equivalent National Insurance contributions thresholds until 5 April 2031 - GOV.UK
thresholds_frozen_until.note: Freeze extended at Budget 2025 (26 November 2025) from 5 April 2028 to 5 April 2031. Covers PA 12,570, basic rate limit 37,700, higher rate threshold 50,270, and the NIC primary threshold / LPL / UEL / UPL.

income_tax_bands_ruk.label: Income tax bands for England, Wales and Northern Ireland (non-savings, non-dividend income)
income_tax_bands_ruk.source_title: Income Tax rates and allowances for current and previous tax years - GOV.UK
income_tax_bands_ruk.note: Expressed on TAXABLE income, i.e. after deducting the (possibly tapered) Personal Allowance. Basic 20% on first 37,700; higher 40% from 37,701 to 125,140; additional 45% above 125,140. With a standard PA this equals gross bands 12,571-50,270 (20%), 50,271-125,140 (40%), over 125,140 (45%). Identical in 2025/26. Wales: Welsh rates of income tax set at 10p in each band for 2026/27, so totals are the same as England/NI (see income_tax_wales). Savings and dividend income use separate UK-wide rates.

basic_rate_limit.label: Basic rate limit (taxable income), rUK
basic_rate_limit.source_title: Income Tax rates and allowances for current and previous tax years - GOV.UK

higher_rate_threshold_gross.label: Gross income at which 40% starts with a standard Personal Allowance (rUK)
higher_rate_threshold_gross.source_title: Income Tax rates and Personal Allowances: Current rates and allowances - GOV.UK
higher_rate_threshold_gross.note: = 12,570 + 37,700. Also equals the Class 4 upper profits limit and the Class 1 upper earnings limit.

additional_rate_threshold.label: Threshold above which the additional (rUK) / top (Scotland) rate applies
additional_rate_threshold.source_title: Income Tax rates and Personal Allowances: Current rates and allowances - GOV.UK
additional_rate_threshold.note: Same figure on taxable and gross income because the PA is nil at 125,140. Some GOV.UK pages write 'over 125,140', others '125,141 and above'; same rule.

income_tax_wales.label: Welsh rates of income tax 2026/27
income_tax_wales.note: Welsh Government kept the Welsh rate at 10p in each band for 2026/27 (Draft Budget written statement 14 October 2025; Final Budget 20 January 2026: https://www.gov.wales/written-statement-draft-budget-2026-27-welsh-taxes). UK rates are reduced by 10p and the Welsh 10p added back, so Welsh taxpayers pay exactly the same as England/NI. Use income_tax_bands_ruk.

income_tax_bands_scotland.label: Scottish income tax bands 2026/27: starter, basic, intermediate, higher, advanced, top (non-savings, non-dividend income)
income_tax_bands_scotland.source_title: Income Tax in Scotland: Current rates - GOV.UK
income_tax_bands_scotland.note: Expressed on TAXABLE income (after the UK Personal Allowance). Derived from the official gross bands for a standard PA of 12,570: starter 12,571-16,537 (19%), basic 16,538-29,526 (20%), intermediate 29,527-43,662 (21%), higher 43,663-75,000 (42%), advanced 75,001-125,140 (45%), top over 125,140 (48%). The starter band 'up to 3,967' on taxable income is confirmed on GOV.UK; the other taxable-income limits are computed by subtracting 12,570 (the advanced/top boundary stays at 125,140 because the PA is nil there). Set at the Scottish Budget of 13 January 2026 (basic and intermediate thresholds +7.4%, higher/advanced/top frozen). Gov.scot: https://www.gov.scot/publications/scottish-income-tax-rates-and-bands/pages/2026-to-2027/. Applies to Scottish taxpayers' earned income (salary, self-employed profits, pensions); savings and dividends use UK rates.

income_tax_bands_scotland_gross_standard.label: Scottish bands 2026/27 as displayed by GOV.UK (TOTAL income, standard Personal Allowance) - for display only
income_tax_bands_scotland_gross_standard.source_title: Income Tax in Scotland: Current rates - GOV.UK
income_tax_bands_scotland_gross_standard.note: Expressed on TOTAL (gross) income assuming the full 12,570 PA. Do not use for computation when income exceeds 100,000 (PA taper): use income_tax_bands_scotland on taxable income instead.

income_tax_bands_scotland_2025_26.label: Scottish income tax bands 2025/26 (previous year)
income_tax_bands_scotland_2025_26.source_title: Income Tax in Scotland: 2025 to 2026 tax year - GOV.UK
income_tax_bands_scotland_2025_26.note: TAXABLE income, computed from the official gross bands: starter 12,571-15,397, basic 15,398-27,491, intermediate 27,492-43,662, higher 43,663-75,000, advanced 75,001-125,140, top over 125,140.

class4_lower_profits_limit.label: Class 4 NIC lower profits limit (LPL)
class4_lower_profits_limit.source_title: Rates and allowances: National Insurance contributions - GOV.UK
class4_lower_profits_limit.note: Same in 2025/26. Frozen with the PA until 5 April 2031.

class4_upper_profits_limit.label: Class 4 NIC upper profits limit (UPL)
class4_upper_profits_limit.source_title: Rates and allowances: National Insurance contributions - GOV.UK

class4_main_rate.label: Class 4 NIC main rate (profits between LPL and UPL)
class4_main_rate.note: 6% since 6 April 2024 (was 9% to 2023/24, 8% planned then cut to 6%). Same in 2025/26. Class 4 is computed on taxable trading profits (no Scottish variation).

class4_additional_rate.label: Class 4 NIC additional rate (profits above UPL)

class2_status.value: Compulsory Class 2 abolished from 6 April 2024. Self-employed people with profits at or above the Small Profits Threshold are treated as having paid Class 2 (State Pension / contributory benefits record protected at no cost). Below the threshold, Class 2 can be paid voluntarily through Self Assessment.
class2_status.label: Class 2 NIC status for the self-employed
class2_status.source_title: A reduction in the main rates of Primary Class 1 and Class 4 National Insurance contributions and the removal of the requirement to pay Class 2 National Insurance contributions - GOV.UK
class2_status.note: From 6 April 2026, voluntary Class 2 can no longer be paid for periods abroad (only Class 3): https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/voluntary-national-insurance-contributions-for-periods-abroad-from-6-april-2026/voluntary-national-insurance-contributions-abroad-from-6-april-2026

class2_small_profits_threshold.label: Class 2 Small Profits Threshold 2026/27 (annual profits)
class2_small_profits_threshold.note: Raised from 6,845 (2025/26) to 7,105 by the Social Security (Contributions) (Rates, Limits and Thresholds Amendments...) Regulations 2026, in force 6 April 2026: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2026/9780348278415/pdfs/ukdsi_9780348278415_en.pdf

uk_register_sole_trader.label: Registering as a sole trader: register for Self Assessment once trading income goes over the trading allowance
uk_register_sole_trader.source_title: Become a sole trader: Register as a sole trader - GOV.UK
uk_register_sole_trader.note: You can start trading straight away. You register as a sole trader by registering for Self Assessment, which you must do if you earn more than £1,000 (trading_allowance) in a tax year (6 April to 5 April), by 5 October after the end of that tax year (sa_registration_deadline). You need a National Insurance number, and can apply for one if you don't have it. Registering late can lead to a penalty. A sole trader runs the business as an individual, keeps all the profits after tax and is personally responsible for any losses the business makes (GOV.UK, What a sole trader is).

more_sources.source_title: Become a sole trader: What a sole trader is - GOV.UK
Self Assessment tax returns: Deadlines - GOV.UK

value: It can't include 'limited', 'Ltd', 'limited liability partnership', 'LLP', 'public limited company' or 'plc'
It can't be the same as an existing trade mark
Sensitive words or expressions, or a name suggesting a connection with government or local authorities, need permission
uk_business_name_rules.label: Sole trader business (trading) name: rules
uk_business_name_rules.source_title: Become a sole trader: Choose your business name - GOV.UK
uk_business_name_rules.note: A business name is any name other than your own. You don't have to register it; registering a trade mark is the way to stop others using it. Your own name and any business name appear on invoices (invoice_requirements_sole_trader).

uk_licences.value: Check whether you need a licence, permit or certification for your activity (for example to play music, sell food or trade in the street) with the GOV.UK licence finder.
uk_licences.label: Licences and permits for a new business

more_sources.source_title: Become a sole trader: What a sole trader is - GOV.UK

uk_licences.note: The sole trader guidance on GOV.UK asks new sole traders to check licences and permits; the finder asks questions about the activity and lists what may be needed. If the finder lists nothing, local councils advise checking with them too.

value: your local council (planning permission and business rates in some cases)
uk_business_from_home.label: Running a business from home: who to check with
uk_business_from_home.source_title: Running a business from home - GOV.UK
uk_business_from_home.note: You may need permission from your mortgage provider or landlord; standard home insurance may not cover business use; a council may require planning permission if the business changes the character of the home, and business rates can apply to a part used only for work. Small business rate relief thresholds differ between pages: not published.

uk_ico_fee.value: Organisations that process personal information, sole traders included, must pay a data protection fee to the Information Commissioner's Office unless they're exempt.
uk_ico_fee.label: ICO data protection fee

more_sources.source_title: Data protection fee self assessment - ICO

uk_ico_fee.note: Exemptions include processing only for staff administration, advertising and marketing your own goods and services, and your own accounts and records; the ICO's self-assessment tool says whether you must pay. Fee amounts differ between ICO pages (older documents show other figures): not published.

uk_records_retention.label: Self-employed records: how long to keep them
uk_records_retention.source_title: Business records if you're self-employed: How long to keep your records - GOV.UK
uk_records_retention.note: Keep records of business income and expenses for at least 5 years after the 31 January submission deadline of the relevant tax year (example: a 2022/23 return sent online by 31 January 2024 means keeping records until at least the end of January 2029). Making Tax Digital records follow the same timeline.

class2_voluntary_weekly_rate.label: Voluntary Class 2 rate 2026/27 (per week)
class2_voluntary_weekly_rate.note: Per week. 3.65 x 52 = 189.80 per year. Share fishermen 4.30/week, volunteer development workers 6.45/week.

class2_voluntary_weekly_rate_2025_26.label: Voluntary Class 2 rate 2025/26 (per week)
class2_voluntary_weekly_rate_2025_26.note: Per week. Payments for a past year are made at that year's rate.

class3_voluntary_weekly_rate.label: Voluntary Class 3 rate 2026/27 (per week)
class3_voluntary_weekly_rate.note: Per week. Builds State Pension entitlement only.

trading_allowance.label: Tax-free trading allowance (gross trading income per tax year)
trading_allowance.source_title: Tax-free allowances on property and trading income - GOV.UK
trading_allowance.note: Gross trading income of 1,000 or less: no need to tell HMRC (unless registered for SA for other reasons). Above 1,000: either deduct the 1,000 allowance OR actual expenses, not both. Cannot create a loss. Covers all trades combined; separate 1,000 property allowance.

simplified_mileage_car_first_10000.label: Simplified expenses flat rate per business mile, cars and goods vehicles, first 10,000 miles (2026/27)
simplified_mileage_car_first_10000.source_title: Simplified expenses if you're self-employed: Vehicles - GOV.UK
simplified_mileage_car_first_10000.note: Re-checked 2026-10-20: 45p to 55p for the first 10,000 business miles from 6 April 2026 (confirmed by the Chancellor in May 2026, backdated), reported by several payroll and accounting sources (Cintra, webexpenses, Clive Owen); GOV.UK page not opened. Per mile. Raised from 45p to 55p, announced 21 May 2026 and retrospective to 6 April 2026 (first change in about 15 years): https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/increase-to-approved-mileage-allowance-payments-amaps-and-self-employed-simplified-mileage-rates. Same figure is the employee AMAP rate. For periods of account not matching the tax year, HMRC guidance requires the rates for each tax year to be applied (exact apportionment wording not verified; see open_questions).

simplified_mileage_car_after_10000.label: Simplified expenses flat rate per business mile, cars and goods vehicles, after 10,000 miles
simplified_mileage_car_after_10000.source_title: Simplified expenses if you're self-employed: Vehicles - GOV.UK
simplified_mileage_car_after_10000.note: Per mile. Unchanged. GOV.UK example: 11,000 miles = 10,000 x 0.55 + 1,000 x 0.25 = 5,750.

simplified_mileage_motorcycle.label: Simplified expenses flat rate per business mile, motorcycles
simplified_mileage_motorcycle.source_title: Simplified expenses if you're self-employed: Vehicles - GOV.UK
simplified_mileage_motorcycle.note: Per mile. Unchanged. Once flat rates are used for a vehicle, they must continue for as long as that vehicle is used in the business. Parking, tolls and congestion charges can be claimed on top.

simplified_mileage_car_first_10000_2025_.label: Simplified mileage rate, cars first 10,000 miles, 2025/26 and earlier
simplified_mileage_car_first_10000_2025_.source_title: Simplified expenses if you're self-employed: Vehicles - GOV.UK
simplified_mileage_car_first_10000_2025_.note: Per mile. Applies to miles driven up to 5 April 2026.

use_of_home_flat_rates.label: Simplified expenses: working from home flat rates (GBP per month)
use_of_home_flat_rates.source_title: Simplified expenses if you're self-employed: Overview - GOV.UK
use_of_home_flat_rates.note: Only if at least 25 hours of business work at home in the month. Covers household running costs (heat, light, power) but not phone/broadband, which are claimed separately on actual business use. Available to sole traders and partnerships with no company partners, not to limited companies. Detailed page: https://www.gov.uk/simpler-income-tax-simplified-expenses/working-from-home

cash_basis_default.value: Since 2024/25 the cash basis is the default accounting basis for sole traders and partnerships of individuals (no turnover entry limit); accruals basis is by election.
cash_basis_default.label: Default accounting basis for the self-employed
cash_basis_default.note: Finance Act 2024 change. Not re-verified against the live page in this session (web search budget exhausted).

sa_registration_deadline.label: Deadline to register for Self Assessment for income first arising in 2026/27
sa_registration_deadline.source_title: Self Assessment tax returns: Deadlines - GOV.UK
sa_registration_deadline.note: Rule: 5 October following the end of the tax year. For 2025/26 income the deadline was 2026-10-05 (already passed). If registered late, HMRC sets a filing deadline 3 months from the date of its notice; payment is still due 31 January.

sa_paper_return_deadline_2025_26.label: Paper Self Assessment return deadline for tax year 2025/26
sa_paper_return_deadline_2025_26.source_title: Self Assessment tax returns: Deadlines - GOV.UK
sa_paper_return_deadline_2025_26.note: Must be received by 23:59 on 31 October.

sa_online_return_deadline_2025_26.label: Online Self Assessment return and balancing payment deadline for tax year 2025/26
sa_online_return_deadline_2025_26.source_title: Self Assessment tax returns: Deadlines - GOV.UK
sa_online_return_deadline_2025_26.note: 23:59 on 31 January 2027. Same day: balancing payment for 2025/26 and first payment on account for 2026/27.

sa_paper_return_deadline.label: Paper Self Assessment return deadline for tax year 2026/27
sa_paper_return_deadline.source_title: Self Assessment tax returns: Deadlines - GOV.UK
sa_paper_return_deadline.note: Rule: 31 October after the end of the tax year. MTD ITSA participants file their final return through software (online deadline applies).

sa_online_return_deadline.label: Online Self Assessment return deadline for tax year 2026/27
sa_online_return_deadline.source_title: Self Assessment tax returns: Deadlines - GOV.UK
sa_online_return_deadline.note: Rule: 31 January after the end of the tax year. Also the MTD ITSA tax return deadline for 2026/27.

sa_balancing_payment_deadline.label: Balancing payment deadline for tax year 2026/27
sa_balancing_payment_deadline.source_title: Self Assessment tax returns: Deadlines - GOV.UK
sa_balancing_payment_deadline.note: Rule: 31 January after the end of the tax year.

payments_on_account_dates.label: Payments on account for tax year 2026/27
payments_on_account_dates.source_title: Understand your Self Assessment tax bill: Payments on account - GOV.UK
payments_on_account_dates.note: Rule: 31 January in the tax year and 31 July after it. For 2025/26 the dates were 2026-01-31 and 2026-07-31.

payments_on_account_fraction.label: Each payment on account as a share of the previous year's Self Assessment liability
payments_on_account_fraction.source_title: Understand your Self Assessment tax bill: Payments on account - GOV.UK
payments_on_account_fraction.note: Two instalments of 50% of the previous year's income tax + Class 4 NIC bill; balance (or repayment) settled on 31 January after the year. Can be reduced if income falls.

payments_on_account_threshold.label: No payments on account if previous year's Self Assessment bill is below this amount
payments_on_account_threshold.source_title: Understand your Self Assessment tax bill: Payments on account - GOV.UK
payments_on_account_threshold.note: Payments on account are not required if last year's SA bill was under 1,000 OR if 80% or more of the total tax was already deducted at source (PAYE, bank interest). Tests apply to the previous year's figures. A June 2026 consultation ('Timely Payments in ITSA') discusses changes, including PAYE-based payments on account from April 2029.

payments_on_account_source_deduction_tes.label: Share of tax deducted at source above which payments on account are not required
payments_on_account_source_deduction_tes.source_title: SALF303 - Payment of tax: payments on account - HMRC internal manual - GOV.UK
payments_on_account_source_deduction_tes.note: 80% or more of the previous year's total income tax assessed deducted at source.

sa_late_filing_penalties.label: Self Assessment late filing penalties (current, non-MTD regime)
sa_late_filing_penalties.source_title: Self Assessment: how to appeal against penalties for late filing and late payment - GOV.UK
sa_late_filing_penalties.note: 100 immediately (even if no tax due or tax paid on time); after 3 months 10/day up to 90 days (900); after 6 months 5% of tax due or 300 if greater. The 12-month penalty (another 5% or 300, higher if information deliberately withheld) is standard GOV.UK guidance (https://www.gov.uk/self-assessment-tax-returns/penalties) but was not re-confirmed in this session. Taxpayers mandated into MTD ITSA from 6 April 2026 move to the points-based regime instead (see mtd_itsa_late_submission_penalty).

sa_late_payment_penalties.label: Self Assessment late payment penalties (current, non-MTD regime): 5% of unpaid tax at each point
sa_late_payment_penalties.source_title: Self Assessment: how to appeal against penalties for late filing and late payment - GOV.UK
sa_late_payment_penalties.note: Plus late payment interest (see hmrc_late_payment_interest_rate). MTD ITSA participants are on the new late payment regime (mtd_itsa_late_payment_penalties).

hmrc_late_payment_interest_rate.label: HMRC late payment interest rate (Self Assessment and most taxes) in force since 9 January 2026
hmrc_late_payment_interest_rate.source_title: HMRC interest rates for late and early payments - GOV.UK
hmrc_late_payment_interest_rate.note: Rule: Bank of England Bank Rate + 4% (margin raised from 2.5% to 4% on 6 April 2025). 3.75% + 4% = 7.75% from 9 January 2026, after the 18 December 2025 Bank Rate cut. Still valid while Bank Rate stays at 3.75%.

hmrc_repayment_interest_rate.label: HMRC repayment interest rate since 9 January 2026
hmrc_repayment_interest_rate.source_title: HMRC interest rates for late and early payments - GOV.UK

mtd_itsa_threshold_2026.label: MTD for Income Tax mandatory from 6 April 2026 if qualifying income exceeds
mtd_itsa_threshold_2026.source_title: Sign up for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - GOV.UK
mtd_itsa_threshold_2026.note: Qualifying income = gross (before expenses) self-employment + property income. For the April 2026 cohort it is measured on the 2024/25 return (2 years before). The threshold itself is confirmed; the 'measured two years earlier' detail comes from GOV.UK guidance that could not be re-read live.

mtd_itsa_threshold_2027.label: MTD for Income Tax mandatory from 6 April 2027 if qualifying income exceeds
mtd_itsa_threshold_2027.source_title: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax for sole traders and landlords: step by step - GOV.UK

mtd_itsa_threshold_2028.label: MTD for Income Tax mandatory from 6 April 2028 if qualifying income exceeds
mtd_itsa_threshold_2028.source_title: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax for sole traders and landlords: step by step - GOV.UK
mtd_itsa_threshold_2028.note: Confirmed on GOV.UK pages; one older GOV.UK page presented this tier as a plan subject to legislation. Based on the 2026/27 tax return.

mtd_itsa_quarterly_deadlines_2026_27.label: MTD for Income Tax quarterly update deadlines, tax year 2026/27
mtd_itsa_quarterly_deadlines_2026_27.source_title: Updates - Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Guidance - GOV.UK
mtd_itsa_quarterly_deadlines_2026_27.note: Standard quarters 6 Apr-5 Jul, 6 Jul-5 Oct, 6 Oct-5 Jan, 6 Jan-5 Apr; calendar quarters (1 Apr-30 Jun etc.) may be elected, same deadlines. Updates are cumulative. Tax return (final declaration) for 2026/27 due 2028-01-31. Next deadline from 2026-10-20: 2026-11-07.

mtd_itsa_late_submission_penalty.label: MTD for Income Tax points-based late submission penalties
mtd_itsa_late_submission_penalty.source_title: Penalties for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - GOV.UK
mtd_itsa_late_submission_penalty.note: 1 point per missed deadline (quarterly update or annual return); 200 penalty when 4 points reached and 200 for each further missed deadline. No points for late quarterly updates during 2026/27 (first year), but the annual return and payments remain penalised. Below threshold, points expire after 24 months. Volunteers have different thresholds.

mtd_itsa_late_payment_penalties.label: MTD for Income Tax late payment penalties
mtd_itsa_late_payment_penalties.source_title: Penalties for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - GOV.UK
mtd_itsa_late_payment_penalties.note: No penalty if paid (or time-to-pay agreed) within 15 days; 16-30 days: % of tax unpaid at day 15; 31+ days: % at day 15 + % at day 30 + annual rate charged daily from day 31 (max 2 years). In the first year a 30-day grace period applies once. The 4% figures for 2027/28 come from the GOV.UK penalties page (corrected 30 March 2026) and should be re-checked.

vat_standard_rate.label: VAT standard rate
vat_standard_rate.note: Default rate for most goods and services.

vat_reduced_rate.label: VAT reduced rate
vat_reduced_rate.note: E.g. domestic energy, children's car seats.

vat_zero_rate.label: VAT zero rate
vat_zero_rate.note: Zero-rated supplies are taxable at 0% (e.g. most food, children's clothes, books); different from exempt supplies.

vat_registration_threshold.label: VAT registration threshold (taxable turnover, rolling 12 months)
vat_registration_threshold.source_title: How VAT works: VAT thresholds - GOV.UK
vat_registration_threshold.note: In force since 1 April 2024 (was 85,000). Budget 2025 Annex A lists 90,000 for April 2026 (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/budget-2025-overview-of-tax-legislation-and-rates-ootlar/annex-a-rates-and-allowances). Register if taxable turnover exceeded 90,000 in the last 12 months, or is expected to exceed it in the next 30 days alone. Voluntary registration possible below. No multi-year freeze commitment found.

vat_deregistration_threshold.label: VAT deregistration threshold
vat_deregistration_threshold.note: In force since 1 April 2024 (was 83,000). Deregistration optional if taxable turnover expected below 88,000 in the next 12 months.

vat_frs_join_threshold.label: VAT Flat Rate Scheme: maximum expected taxable turnover to join (excluding VAT)
vat_frs_join_threshold.source_title: VAT Flat Rate Scheme: Overview - GOV.UK

vat_frs_leave_threshold.label: VAT Flat Rate Scheme: must leave if total income exceeds (including VAT)
vat_frs_leave_threshold.source_title: VAT Flat Rate Scheme: If your circumstances change - GOV.UK
vat_frs_leave_threshold.note: Checked on each anniversary of joining (last 12 months or expected next 12 months, including VAT) or if income in the next 30 days alone is expected above 230,000. May stay with HMRC agreement if expected to fall below 191,500. Must wait 12 months before rejoining.

vat_frs_limited_cost_trader_rate.label: VAT Flat Rate Scheme: limited cost business rate
vat_frs_limited_cost_trader_rate.source_title: VAT Flat Rate Scheme: Work out your flat rate - GOV.UK
vat_frs_limited_cost_trader_rate.note: Limited cost business = VAT-inclusive spend on relevant goods below 2% of VAT-inclusive turnover, or above 2% but below 1,000 a year. Excludes capital items, food/drink for the business or staff, vehicles, vehicle parts and fuel. Applied to VAT-inclusive turnover. Most service freelancers with low goods costs fall into this category, making the FRS rarely advantageous for them.

vat_frs_first_year_discount.label: VAT Flat Rate Scheme: reduction in the first year of VAT registration
vat_frs_first_year_discount.source_title: VAT Flat Rate Scheme: Work out your flat rate - GOV.UK
vat_frs_first_year_discount.note: 1 percentage point off the flat rate until the day before the first anniversary of VAT registration (limited cost business: 15.5%). Lost if joining the scheme late.

vat_return_deadline.value: 1 calendar month and 7 days after the end of the VAT accounting period (usually quarterly), submitted through MTD-compatible software; payment due the same day.
vat_return_deadline.label: VAT return and payment deadline
vat_return_deadline.note: Standard rule, not re-verified against the live page in this session. MTD for VAT applies to all VAT-registered businesses since April 2022.

value: Business name, address and contact information of the supplier
Name (company name) and address of the customer
Clear description of what is being charged for

invoice_requirements_all.label: What every UK invoice must include

vat_invoice_full_requirements.label: Full VAT invoice requirements
vat_invoice_full_requirements.note: Required for standard- or reduced-rated supplies to another VAT-registered business when the VAT-inclusive value exceeds 250 (or on request). A 'modified' invoice (VAT-inclusive values) may be used if the customer agrees. Items 1 to 11 re-checked on 2026-10-21 against search excerpts of VAT Notice 700 (section 16.3), HMRC manual VATREC5010 and the Value Added Tax Regulations 1995, regulation 14 (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1995/2518/regulation/14): the discount item is the rate of any cash discount offered, and the invoice date is required where it differs from the time of supply. The time of supply (tax point) can differ from the date the goods or services were provided: an earlier invoice or payment, or an invoice issued soon after the supply, sets it (Notice 700, time of supply). Item 12 (reverse charge, zero-rate or exempt wording) not confirmed by those excerpts. A VAT invoice is normally issued within 30 days of the supply. See also https://www.gov.uk/guidance/record-keeping-for-vat-notice-70021 Amounts on a VAT invoice may be expressed in any currency (VAT Regulations 1995, regulation 14, as quoted in search excerpts), but the total VAT must be shown in sterling.

ir35_summary.value:
IR35 (the 'off-payroll working rules', Chapters 8 and 10 of Part 2 ITEPA 2003) applies when a contractor provides services to a client through an intermediary, usually their own personal service limited company, and would be an employee of the client if engaged directly (control, personal service/no real substitution, mutuality of obligation). If the engagement is 'inside IR35', the income must be taxed broadly like employment income: income tax and employee and employer Class 1 NIC, with no tax advantage from dividends. Sole traders invoicing in their own name are not under IR35, although their employment status can still be challenged.

Who decides depends on the client. For public sector clients and for medium or large private/voluntary sector clients, the client must determine status, issue a Status Determination Statement with reasons, and the fee-payer (client or agency) deducts PAYE and NIC; the contractor can challenge it through the client's disagreement process (45-day response). For small private sector clients, the contractor's own company decides and accounts for any deemed employment payment itself. A company is small if it meets at least two of: turnover not over 15 million, balance sheet total not over 7.5 million, 50 employees or fewer (thresholds for financial years beginning on or after 6 April 2025). HMRC's CEST tool helps assess status.
ir35_summary.label: IR35 / off-payroll working rules: plain summary
ir35_summary.note: Client guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/off-payroll-working-for-clients ; size thresholds from 6 April 2025: https://www.gov.uk/hmrc-internal-manuals/employment-status-manual/esm10006a (older pages still show 10.2m / 5.1m).
